hypothesis: Two-sided reward-scoring asks from complete sets on Polymarket rewarded markets earn liquidity rewards larger than the adverse selection on the asks that fill.
evidence_before: Snapshot estimates only (runs/p15/reward_est.json); no reward P&L has been measured. The 3-minute smoke run is excluded from the test.
session: one live paper session of 4 h, started after this file is committed; k=30 markets chosen by reward_farm.select(max_min_size=50, min_hours=48) at the session start
metric: per market: equity at session end / capital (USDC split), equity = cash from fills + unsold pairs x 1 + held outcome x best BID + accrued rewards - capital
pass_rule: mean per-market return > 0 with t > 2.0 across the 30 markets (one market per event, so markets are independent clusters) AND the 100 USD account (the first markets in selection order whose capital sums to <= 100 USD) ends with net USD > 0. Reported but not used to pass: mid-marked equity.
caveats: rewards are computed with the published formula against the visible book (multiplier b = 1, no knowledge of other makers' identities, which overstates competitors' Q and understates ours); held outcomes are not resolved within the session.
